**Revised Narrative**

The most strongly enriched pathway in this dataset is **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism** (KEGG map00260; FDR ≈ 0, fold-enrichment ≈ 569), which clusters five of the ten input metabolites: 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109), (R)-Lipoic acid (C16241), S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), L-Cysteine (C00097), and L-Methionine (C00073). [retracted: Ornithine (C00077) is incorrectly assigned to this pathway per KEGG map00260 composition; it belongs to the urea cycle instead.] A secondary hit with FDR ≈ 0 and fold-enrichment ≈ 131 is the Reactome **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives** pathway, which encompasses the same core sulfur–amino-acid module and adds 1-Pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (C03912) and 5,6-Dihydroxyindole (C05578).

L-Methionine (C00073) is a confirmed member of Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism, and KEGG reaction-path tracing confirms a reachable path from L-Methionine to L-Cysteine (C00097) via cystathionine intermediates (4 hops). L-Cysteine, in turn, connects to S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) through S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) cycle intermediates (4 hops). Ornithine (C00077) links these metabolites to the urea cycle, providing nitrogen-handling context. [retracted: (R)-Lipoic acid is a cofactor in oxidative decarboxylation reactions that interface with the pyruvate/2-oxobutanoate node of this network] (R)-Lipoic acid (C16241) is an established cofactor in oxidative decarboxylation reactions, while 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109) is a branch-point intermediate in methionine catabolism. Phenylephrine (C07441) is likely an adrenergic signal unrelated to the sulfur-amino axis; it may reflect systemic stress or cardiovascular tone changes.

Collectively, the data point to a **disruption of amino-acid metabolism**, plausibly through altered methionine utilization and interconnected sulfur-amino-acid flux. S-Adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) is also reported in RaMP-DB to belong to Meiosis, Drug ADME, and DNA Repair pathways; the observed elevation may therefore reflect broader methyl-group transfer demands beyond amino-acid cycling.

**Limitations**
RaMP-DB does not annotate a discrete "SAM cycle" or "transsulfuration cycle" pathway; "catecholamine-derived pigment pathway" was also not recovered in enrichment hits. Claims involving these non-annotated routes are retracted or dropped. Ornithine's assignment to Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism was also contradicted and is removed. Additional experimental validation is required before attributing antioxidant or nitrogen-detoxification consequences.
